slot_note: first realisation of analytical_tasks note DS02; the note's decisive rung (drains per window built from the capacity register, the hourly forecast and the window calendar) is kept as the stop rung, and a new decisive rung, what one drain of a colocated host actually takes out when the provider rebuilds the host from the estate's current platform image, sits above it
niche: an online travel platform's vulnerability office splitting the patch crews' monthly change tickets across two colocated and four cloud production estates, sized by the exploitable host exposures the tickets take out in November when the colocation provider can drain only so many hosts a window and rebuilds every host it drains
answer: Give payments 4 tickets, checkout 5, search 72, media 75, internal tools 77 and the data pipeline 67, which takes out 13,300 exploitable host exposures in November.
stakeholder_role: remediation planner in the vulnerability management office of an online travel platform, who splits the patch crews' 300 monthly change tickets across six production estates

spine.entity: one open vulnerability finding, one CVE on one installed package on one host
spine.source: synthetic (fictional scanner export over CVE-format identifiers; exploit-prediction scores shaped on FIRST's public EPSS feed, constructed case under CC BY 4.0 as the pack's provenance record states)

world.org_type: online travel booking platform with a colocated payments platform and four cloud estates

driver: The decisive quantity is how many requests it takes to spend a binding resource whose budget is stated for the whole period, because each request draws only on the capacity of the one interval it is booked into; a plan that values every use correctly but files one request against the period's whole budget reaches one interval's share, so the constrained candidates need one request per interval and the unconstrained candidates give up that many places under the cap.
driver_concrete: A colocated ticket rides one provider change request and a request is for one window, so each November window drains 24 hosts under its own ticket: payments needs 4 tickets and checkout 5 to spend 96 and 120 drains on the most exposed hosts, and the cloud estates keep 291 tickets, not 298; every past colocated ticket in the crew log carries exactly one change request and the part-accepted ones never reached their declined hosts.
stump: A competent solver recovers the cut-day scoring rule, builds 96 and 120 drains from the window-hours headroom, finds that a drained host comes back on the current image and files one glibc ticket per colocated estate naming the 96 and 120 most exposed hosts: 1 / 1 / 74 / 77 / 79 / 68 for about 13,360; the step that lands it there is spending a whole month's drains under one ticket, when a ticket is one change request and a request is for one window, so the split is 4 / 5 / 72 / 75 / 77 / 67 for 13,300.

lineage.architecture: v1 (harden loop 0): whole-host rebuild valuation as the decisive rung, one colocated ticket spending the month's drains
lineage.fate: solved by the in-house plain solver in round 1 (2026-10-10); kept as the stop rung of loop 1
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what one use of the binding resource removes, which is everything on the member that the current baseline fixes rather than the single item the request names, because each use rebuilds the member from that baseline; a ledger that credits each request with its own item reproduces every closed period, so per-item valuation spends the scarce uses on the members with the richest single item instead of the members carrying the most in total, and the constrained candidates need far fewer requests for far more removal than the per-item reading allows.
